sample: 40 of 224 strings, batch index floor(i*224/40) for i=0..39 (about every 5.6th string), translated on my own in rev033/mine.json (rev033/mine.py) before I opened out/033.json
notes: No meaning disagreement in the 40 sampled strings, so out/033.json is unchanged (byte-identical to rev033/033.before.json). Every number, unit and code survives verbatim (-40℃/90℃, 106 x 156 x (2.5-3.2) mm, 3x5mm, 2m, 1PCS, NFC, 3D). Warnings and limitations are kept: hot liquids «can damage… reduce its lifespan, or cause burns», «discontinue use immediately until the device is fully repaired», «DO NOT attempt to use or charge… leakage or corrosion», «Please be cautious of the interference…», and the oil-stain note «not a fault or quality issue». Glossary terms match (حزمة البطارية/کۆمەڵە باتری, مادة مجففة/ماددەی وشککەرەوە, عزم الدوران/تۆرک, مسمار توجيه/بزمار for the dowel pin, غير مرفق/لەگەڵدا نییە, تعليمات استخدام نموذج 3D/ڕێنماییەکانی بەکارهێنانی مۆدێلی 3D). Names stay Latin and verbatim (BreezeBuddy, Halloween Ghost Night Light, Endless Loop Express, Apex Legends Wingman with Reload Mechanics, Electric Water Spray Kit 01, Electric Water Toy Gun, Cipher Helmet Lock, Maker's Supply, MakerWorld). No Sorani row copies the Arabic.

My own version was the wrong one in 8 places, so none of them counts against the first translation. (1) «non-3D printed parts» (indices 106, 123, 140, 179, 196, 218) and «3D-printed objects» (89): I followed the glossary phrase «القطع غير المطبوعة بطابعة 3D» / «ئەو پارچانەی بە 3D چاپ ناکرێن». The validator treats «non-3D» and «3D-printed» as protected CODE_TOKENs (a digit plus a capital letter), so my rows fail with TOKEN_LOST, as rev033/chk/check.ts shows: 7 of my rows fail. The first translation keeps them as «(non-3D)» / «(3D-printed)» and passes. The glossary entry «3D printed parts» should say that «non-3D» must survive verbatim. (2) Index 151: I translated «Transparent». But «3x5mm Transparent 2m (1PCS)» is an option value of the Silicone Tubes product (SKU B-RC021; row 180 cites it with «- RC021»), so it stays English, as the first translation has it.

Choices that are not disagreements: index 16 «2PCS：106 x 156 x （2.5-3.2）mm» is kept English as a size cell in the first translation, and I wrote «2 قطعة» / «2 دانە». Either is acceptable. Index 84: the first translation writes «توافق واسع: يعمل بالكامل مع…» rather than «متوافق تمامًا مع», which avoids repeating «compatibility» in one line (glossary: say compatibility once). The meaning is the same. Head nouns added before names («فانوس»/«مصباح» before Halloween Classic Carved Pumpkin Lantern, Halloween Ghost Light and the TheeLight, «پەڕەی» before the MakerWorld page) only clarify and change no fact.

Whole-file checks (not limited to the sample): all 188 translated rows pass validateTranslationRow (feat/import-i18n worktree, names.json plus IDENTITY_TERMS): ok 188, bad 0. No Sorani row contains an Arabic-only letter (ة ث ذ ض ظ ط ي ك ى). The 36 keep rows are all names: MakerWorld model titles, creator handles, the comparison-table product labels «CMYK Backlight Board» and «Lithophane LED Backlight Board （2PCS/4PCS）», plus the size cell at index 16. None of them is an English sentence left untranslated.
